name: London Underground
amount_note: £100 on all six TfL modes, reduced to £50 if paid within 21 days of the notice being issued. After a failed stage-one appeal the £50 window re-opens for 21 days from the rejection letter, then reverts to £100.
deadline_note: Appeal at stage one within 21 days beginning the day after the DATE OF TRAVEL - not the notice date; stages two and three within 14 days of the date of the previous rejection letter. No decision deadline is published for any stage.
stages_note: Three policy stages, none of the first two independent of TfL: stage one is decided by the Independent Appeals Service (IAS/IRCAS), a contractor TfL says considers appeals on its behalf in accordance with TfL guidelines; stage two by the Appeals and Prosecutions Team in TfL's own Security, Policing and Enforcement directorate; stage three by the Independent Appeals Panel - appointed by TfL, required by the policy to work within TfL's regulations, policy and processes, and whose decision TfL states binds it.
instrument_note: Greater London Authority Act 1999, s.245 and Schedule 17 (as amended by the Transport for London Act 2008), administered under TfL's Penalty Fare Appeals Policy, version 11 (November 2025) - the policy is TfL's own document, not legislation.
source: TfL, "Penalty fares and how to pay them"; TfL Penalty Fare Appeals Policy, version 11 (November 2025); Greater London Authority Act 1999, Schedule 17

name: Manchester Metrolink
amount_note: £120 - Metrolink calls it a "Standard Fare (Penalty Fare)" (conditions of carriage, condition 7) - halved to £60 if paid within 14 days of receipt; the full amount is due within 21 days.
deadline_note: Appeal within 21 days of receiving the notice (the conditions of carriage put it at 21 days of issue). Metrolink says it aims to reply with a decision within 14 days - an aim, not a deadline.
stages_note: One internal review only, run for TfGM by KAM Revenue Recovery. Metrolink states it accepts appeals only in exceptional circumstances; no external or independent stage exists.
instrument_note: Metrolink's own conditions of carriage (condition 7); the Metrolink byelaws are made under the Greater Manchester (Light Rapid Transit System) Acts 1988. Not SI 2018/366 and not the TfL scheme - neither applies here.

name: Nottingham Express Transit
amount_note: £120, halved to £60 if paid within 14 days; a £30 administration charge is added if it is still unpaid after 22 days.
deadline_note: The appeal form must be completed within 22 days of the penalty being issued - the same 22-day window as paying in full before the £30 charge. No decision deadline is published.
stages_note: One internal review only. NET accepts appeals only in exceptional circumstances, or with evidence that a ticket for the whole journey was bought and completed before boarding; no external or independent stage exists.
instrument_note: NET's own published conditions and penalty fares process. Not SI 2018/366 and not the TfL scheme - neither applies here.
source: NET, "Penalty fares"

name: West Midlands Metro
amount_note: West Midlands Metro's own documents disagree: £100 per its ticketing terms and conditions (halved if paid within 14 days, due within 28 days of issue), but £10 per its published penalty fares scheme document, citing s.5(1) of the Midland Metro (Penalty Fares) Act 1991. Both are its own publications; both are stated here.
deadline_note: Its documents disagree here too: appeal within 21 days beginning the day after issue per the scheme document, or at any point within the 28-day period per the terms and conditions. The safest reading is 21 days. The scheme document says a received appeal suspends the payment period until a decision is made, and promises a stage-one decision within 14 days.
stages_note: Two internal stages: the Network Manager, then - within 14 days of a stage-one rejection - the Operator's Panel (the Head of Operations and the Metro Customer Services Manager), whose decision is final. Neither stage is independent of the operator.
instrument_note: Midland Metro (Penalty Fares) Act 1991, ss.4 and 5(1), and the operator's published appeals process and ticketing terms. Not SI 2018/366 and not the TfL scheme.
source: West Midlands Metro, "Penalty fare appeals process"
